applied_settings: ***TUNED - Afterburner Profile 4 (fulltune), memory +2500, power limit 111% = 200 W. NOT STOCK.*** LEG 4 OF 4 IN AN ABBA DOSE-RESPONSE RUN, tag a2. PURPOSE: the paper claims frequency reduction and undervolting are SUBSTITUTES drawing on one pool of headroom, evidenced by two points - stock leaves 55.9% recoverable by dropping frequency, the split curve leaves 27.5%. Profile 4 is a third point whose DOSE IS MEASURED: it draws 11.4% less power than Profile 5 across 1237-2010 MHz at matched achieved clock (26.9% at 2010 MHz), so it is unambiguously the deeper undervolt. The prediction under test is that its remaining headroom falls BELOW 27.5%. ORDER IS ABBA (fulltune, split, split, fulltune) because that cancels linear session drift exactly - both configurations are centred on the same instant - whereas ABAB would load any monotonic drift onto the comparison. Every other cross-configuration comparison in this repository is day-1 vs day-2 and carries the ~1.47% cross-session drift CLAUDE.md records for a single unchanged configuration; this design removes it. A COOLDOWN PRECEDES EVERY LEG - 12 min floor, 40 C target, 25 min ceiling - so all four legs start from a comparable cooled card; this leg began at 33 C. An earlier version ran the legs back to back on the reasoning that identical WARM starts hold thermal state constant, which was wrong: leg 1 starts from an idle-cold card while later legs would start hot off the preceding sweep, putting the asymmetry on a1 - one half of the very bracket the drift estimate is built from. CONFIGURATION IDENTIFIED BY MEASUREMENT, NOT BY SLOT NUMBER: memory clock under load 16301 MHz, and - the check that actually separates the two profiles - mean power 73.4 W at a locked 2010 MHz against 79.5 W expected for fulltune and 108.8 W for the other profile. The top-of-grid achieved clock CANNOT distinguish them - full tune ~2948 and split ~2977 are ~29 MHz apart, inside thermal variation - and an identity probe relying on it on 2026-09-08 was ambiguous. Power at matched clock separates them by 27%. Profile 4 was confirmed to be the full tune the same day by its matched-frequency power curve, which reproduces the -18% to -26% CLAUDE.md records for that configuration on gemm. Driver 616.64. Operator away from the machine; curve applied programmatically. A display-driver crash watcher ran alongside, logging Event ID 4101 and nvlddmkm entries and polling for silent offset loss. WARNING: a driver reset SILENTLY CLEARS the Afterburner offsets, so a sweep after such an event would measure stock under this string - the per-sweep achieved clocks and the watcher log are the check.
